    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    The expression is false.

    −(A∠ θ)=A ∠ (−θ)

    −(A ∠ θ)=A ∠ θ+180°

    #Part (b)

    The expression is false. Since both vectors have the same angle from the positive
    x-axis, the cross product would thus be zero as A×B=ABsinϕ where ϕ is
    the angle between the two vectors.

    #Part (c)

    The expression is false. The dot product of two vectors gives a scalar.

    (A ∠ θ)⋅(B ∠ θ)=ABcos0=AB

    #Part (d)

    The expression is true.

    −(B ∠ θ)=B ∠ θ+180°

    A ∠ θ+B ∠ θ+180°=A ∠ θ−B ∠ θ

    A ∠ θ+B ∠ θ+180°=(A−B) ∠ θ

    #Part (e)

    The expression is false. The cross product is in the direction of −k^.

    (A ∠ θ)×(B ∠ θ−2π​)=−ABk^

    #Question 1

    A translating reference system attached to a point only moves (translates) with the point
    and does not rotate with the point, thus orientation of the     x- and y-axis is unchanged.

    Absolute motion of A and B rotate in concentric circles about the fixed point O.

    Point B moves in an anticlockwise circular motion with A at its center.

    Point O moves in an anticlockwise circular motion with B at its center.

    Relative motion of A with respect to the disk is zero.

    #Tutorial 3 (Planar Curvilinear Motion)

    #Question 1

    Let the initial height of the target be H.

    Let the height of the target on impact be y2​.

    Let the height of the projectile on impact be y1​.

    Height of Projectile on Impact

    v0x​=v0​cosθ

    v0y​=v0​sinθ

    L=(v0​cosθ)t

    y=y0​+v0y​t+21​at2

    y1​=(v0​sinθ)t−21​gt2

    Height of Target on Impact

    y=y0​+v0​t+21​at2

    −(H−y2​)=−21​gt2

    y2​=H−21​gt2

    tanθ=LH​

    H=Ltanθ

    H=cosθ(v0​cosθ)t⋅sinθ​

    H=(v0​sinθ)t

    y2​=(v0​sinθ)t−21​gt2

    Since y1​=y2​, the projectile hits the target.

    #Question 5

    Let the vertical height of the rocket from B be h.

    tanθ=bh​

    h=btanθ

    Velocity of rocket is the rate of change of h with respect to t.

    Since angle θ is also a function of t, we need to apply chain rule.

    v=dtd​ btanθ

    v=b dtd​tanθ

    v=b dθd​tanθ⋅dtdθ​

    v=b(sec2θ)θ˙

    Acceleration of the rocket is the rate of change of v with respect to t.

    Thus, we need to apply the product rule for differentiation.

    a=dtd​ b(sec2θ)θ˙

    a=b dtd​(secθ)2θ˙

    a=b[θ¨(sec2θ)+θ˙dtd​(secθ)2]

    a=b[θ¨(sec2θ)+θ˙⋅2(secθ)(secθtanθ)(dtdθ​)]

    a=b[θ¨(sec2θ)+2θ˙2sec2θtanθ]

    a=b(sec2θ)θ¨+2b(sec2θtanθ)θ˙2

    #Question 6

    #Part (a)

    Taking A-x′-y′ as the reference frame.

    Isosceles △OBA

    ∠ OAB=180−2θ

    Isosceles △EBA

    ∠ BAE=ϕ

    ∠ BAE=180−∠ OAB

    ∠ BAE=180−(180−2θ)

    ∠ BAE=2θ

    ∴ ϕ=2θ and ϕ˙​=2θ˙

    ∴  Since θ˙ is a constant, θ¨=0. Thus, ϕ¨​=0.

    Acceleration of B in reference frame A-x′-y′

    aB​=(r¨−rθ˙2)er​+(rθ¨+2r˙θ˙)eθ​

    aB​=(r¨−rϕ˙​2)er​+(rϕ¨​+2r˙ϕ˙​)eϕ​

    Since B rotates in a circular motion about A with a fixed radius, r˙=r¨=0.

    Acceleration equation becomes aB​=(−rϕ˙​2)er​=(−bϕ˙​2)er​.

    aB​=(−bϕ2)er​

    aB​=[−b(2θ˙)2]er​

    aB​=(−4bθ˙2)er​

    aB​=−4bθ˙2 ∠ ϕ

    aB​=4bθ˙2 ∠ ϕ+180°

    #Part (b)

    Taking O-x-y as the reference frame.

    vB​=r˙er​+rθ˙eθ​

    aB​=(r¨−rθ˙2)er​+(rθ¨+2r˙θ˙)eθ​

    Expressing r in terms of θ.

    r=2bcosθ

    Differentiating with respect to t.

    r˙=2b(−sinθ)⋅dtdθ​=−2bθ˙sinθ

    r¨=−2b[θ¨sinθ+θ˙cosθ⋅dtdθ​]

    r¨=−2b(θ¨sinθ+θ˙2cosθ)

    Velocity Relative to Rotating Rod OC

    vB​=rθ˙eθ​+r˙er​

    vB​=vOC​+vB/OC​

    where vB​ is the absolute velocity of B with respect to O,
    and vOC​ is the entrained velocity due to rotation of the rod,
    and     vB/OC​ is the relative velocity of B with respect to the rod.

    vB/OC​=r˙er​

    vB/OC​=(−2bθ˙sinθ)er​

    Acceleration Relative to Rotating Rod OC

    aB​=(r¨−rθ˙2)er​+(rθ¨+2r˙θ˙)eθ​

    aB​=(rθ¨eθ​−rθ˙2er​)+r¨er​+2r˙θ˙eθ​

    aB​=aOC​+aB/OC​+acoriolis​

    where aB​ is the absolute acceleration of B with respect to O,
    and aOC​ is the entrained acceleration due to rotation of the rod,
    and     aB/OC​ is the relative acceleration of B with respect to the rod.

    The two terms in aOC​ represent the tangential and normal acceleration,
    where     rθ¨=rα is the tangential acceleration,
    and     rθ˙2=rω2 is the normal acceleration.

    aB/OC​=r¨er​

    aB/OC​=[−2b(θ¨sinθ+θ˙2cosθ)]er​

    walled hollow cylinder is     I=mr2.

    As the pipe is rolling down the ramp, the ramp is also moving towards the right.

    Thus, absolute acceleration of the pipe is given by aP​=aR​+aP/R​.

    Resolving the equation into en​- and et​-components,

    aP​=aR​i−aP/R​et​

    aP​=−aR​sin30°en​+aR​cos30°et​−aP/R​et​

    aP​=(−21​aR​)en​+(23​​aR​−aP/R​)et​

    Using Newton’s second law on the pipe,

    maP​=N1​en​−Ffr​et​−mgj

    500aP​=N1​en​−Ffr​et​+500g(−cos30°en​−sin30°et​)

    500aP​=(N1​−250g3​)en​+(−Ffr​−250g)et​

    Comparing the en​- and et​-components,

    500(−21​aR​)=N1​−250g3​

    −250aR​=N1​−250g3​     −[1]

    500(23​​aR​−aP/R​)=−Ffr​−250g

    (2503​)aR​−500aP/R​=−Ffr​−250g

    (2503​)aR​−500aP/R​=500aP/R​−250g

    −433aR​+1000aP/R​=2452.5     −[2]

    Using Newton’s second law on the ramp,

    maR​=N2​ j−N1​en​+Ffr​et​−mgj

    300aR​=N2​ j+N1​(sin30°i−cos30°j)+Ffr​(cos30°i+sin30°j)−300gj

    300aR​=(21​N1​+23​​Ffr​)i+(N2​−300g−23​​N1​+21​Ffr​)j

    Comparing the i- and j-components,

    300aR​=21​N1​+23​​Ffr​     −[3]

    0=N2​−300g−23​​N1​+21​Ffr​

    Substituting Ffr​=−500aP/R​ into [3],

    300aR​=21​N1​+23​​(−500aP/R​)

    600aR​=N1​−866aP/R​

    N1​=600aR​+866aP/R​

    Substituting N1​ into [1],

    −250aR​=600aR​+866aP/R​−250g3​

    850aR​=250g3​−866aP/R​

    aR​=5−1.0188aP/R​     [4]

    Substituting [4] into [2],

    −433(5−1.0188aP/R​)+1000aP/R​=2452.5

    −2165+441.14aP/R​+1000aP/R​=2452.5

    aP/R​=3.2041 m/s2

    aR​=1.7357 m/s2

    #Conservation of Energy

    Let h be the initial height of the pipe.

    mP​gh=21​mP​vP​2+21​IP​ω2+21​mR​vR​2

    mP​gh=21​mP​vP​2+21​IP​(0.5vP/R​​)2+21​mR​vR2​

    500(9.81)h=21​(500)vP​2+21​(500)(0.5)2(0.5vP/R​​)2+21​(300)vR​2

    4905h=250vP​2+250vP/R​2+150vR​2     −[1]

    vP​=vR​+vP/R​

    vP​=vR​i+vP/R​(−cos30°i−sin30°j)

    vP​=(vR​−23​​vP/R​)i+(−21​vP/R​)j

    vP​2=vP​⋅vP​

    vP​2=(vR​−23​​vP/R​)2+(−21​vP/R​)2

    vP​2=vR​2−3​vR​vP/R​+43​vP/R​2+41​vP/R​2

    vP​2=vR​2−3​vR​vP/R​+vP/R​2     −[2]

    Using conservation of momentum in the i-direction,

    0=mP​vP​+mR​vR​

    0=500(vR​−23​​vP/R​)+300vR​

    2503​vP/R​=800vR​

    vR​=1653​​vP/R​

    aR​=1653​​aP/R​

    Substituting the above into [2],

    vP​2=(1653​​)2vP/R​2−3​(1653​​)vP/R​2+vP/R​2

    vP​2=25675​vP/R​2−1615​vP/R​2+vP/R​2

    vP​2=25691​vP/R​2

    Substituting the above into [1],

    4905h=250(25691​)vP/R​2+250vP/R​2+150(1653​​)2vP/R​2

    4905h=382.81vP/R​2

    Let s be the displacement of the pipe along the ramp.

    4905⋅s(sin30°)=382.81vP/R​2

    2452.5s=382.81vP/R​2

    Displacement of the pipe along the ramp is a linear motion.

    Using kinematic equation vf​2=vi​2+2a(sf​−si​),

    vP/R​2=2aP/R​s

    2452.5s=382.81(2aP/R​)s

    aP/R​=3.2033 m/s2

    aP​=1653​​(3.2033)

    aP​=1.7338 m/s2

    #Question 6

    L=xD​+2xB​

    0=aD​+2aB​

    aD​=−2aB​

    aG​=rα=0.15α

    aD​=2(0.15)α=0.3α

    where α is angular acceleration of disk w.r.t. the contact point on the ground

    Using principle of angular momentum,
    and taking anticlockwise as positive,

    MG​=IG​α

    (Ffr​−T)0.15=21​(9.8150​)(0.15)2α

    Ffr​−T=21​(9.8150​)(0.15)0.3aD​​

    Ffr​=1.2742aD​+T

    Ffr​=−2.5484aB​+T     −[1]

    Using Newton’s second law on the disk,

    Ffr​+T=−mD​aG​

    Ffr​+T=−9.8150​(21​aD​)

    Ffr​+T=−2.5484aD​

    Ffr​+T=−2.5484(−2aB​)

    Ffr​+T=5.0968aB​     −[2]

    Using Newton’s second law on the block,

    mg−2T=mB​aB​

    20−2T=9.8120​aB​

    20−2T=2.0387aB​     −[3]

    Acceleration of Block

    Substituting [1] into [2],

    −2.5484aB​+2T=5.0968aB​

    2T=7.6452aB​

    Substituting 2T=7.6452aB​ into [3],

    20−7.6452aB​=2.0387aB​

    aB​=2.0653 m/s2

    Coefficient of Static Friction

    T=27.6452(2.0653)​

    T=7.8948 N

    Ffr​=−2.5484aB​+T

    Ffr​=−2.5484(2.0653)+7.8948

    Ffr​=2.6315 N

    μs​=NFfr​​=502.6315​=0.052631

    #Question 3

    Taking rotation of the rod about the instantaneous center C,

    IC​=IG​+mrG/C​2

    IC​=121​mL2+m(21​L)2

    IC​=31​mL2

    By taking rotation about C, we can eliminate the need to determine translational kinetic energy of the rod as it only rotates about C. Thus, the rod only has rotational kinetic
    energy. Apply the parallel axis theorem to find its new mass moment of inertia.

    Using conservation of energy,

    mgh=21​kh2+21​mvG​2+21​IG​ω2

    mgh=21​kh2+21​m(rG/C​⋅ω)2+21​IG​ω2

    mgh=21​kh2+21​(IG​+mrG/C​2)ω2

    mgh=21​kh2+21​IC​ω2

    mg(Lsinθ)=21​k(Lsinθ)2+21​(31​mL2)ω2

    Substituting in the given values,

    12(9.81)(0.75sinθ)=21​(120)(0.75)2sin2θ+61​(12)(0.75)2ω2

    88.29sinθ−33.75sin2θ=1.125ω2

    ω=78.48sinθ−30sin2θ​

    vA​=rA/C​⋅ω

    vA​=±0.75cosθ78.48sinθ−30sin2θ​

    The plus-minus sign indicates that the A can be moving either upwards or downwards.

    #Question 4

    Rotation about instantaneous center,

    vG(wheel)​=rω=0.075ω

    vG(carriage)​=2rω=0.15ω

    Friction between the wheels and the ground does no work. At the point of contact
    between the wheel and the ground, there is no relative motion between them,
    thus friction does no work. Friction between the wheels and the carriage are
    internal forces and cancel each other out.

    Using work and kinetic energy principle,
    and letting s be the displacement of the carriage,

    W=10s

    ΔKE=ΔKEcarriage​+ΔKEwheels​

    ΔKE=21​mc​vG(carriage)​2+2(21​mw​vG(wheel)​2+21​IG​ω2)

    ΔKE=21​mc​vc​2+mw​vw​2+IG​ω2

    ΔKE=21​mc​vc​2+mw​(rw​ω)2+IG​ω2

    ΔKE=21​mc​vc​2+(IG​+mw​rw​2)ω2

    ΔKE=21​mc​vc​2+IIC​ω2

    ΔKE=21​mc​vc​2+IIC​(0.15vc​​)2

    Using parallel axis theorem,

    IIC​=21​mw​rw​2+mw​rw​2

    IIC​=21​(4)(0.075)2+4(0.075)2

    IIC​=0.03375 kg⋅m2

    ΔKE=21​(6)vc​2+0.1520.03375​vc​2

    ΔKE=4.5vc​2

    Forming the work-energy equation,

    10s=4.5vc​2

    Using kinematic equation vf​2=vi​2+2a(sf​−si​),

    vc​2=2ac​s

    Substituting the above into the work-energy equation,

    10s=4.5(2ac​s)

    ac​=1.1111 m/s

    Using kinematic equation vf​=vi​+at,

    vc​=ac​t

    vc​=1.1111(2.5)

    vc​=2.7778 m/s
